intro: A city builds a chalet for a man with a mustache when the man it is modeled on once lived 40 days on the scoreboard to prove anyone would show up, and Milwaukee has never quite stopped being grateful.

mascots.name: Bernie Brewer
mascots.tagline: Lederhosen, a 75-foot slide, and one espionage charge

facts.fact: Milt Mason, the retired aviation engineer who became the first Bernie, had a color TV, a gas stove, a refrigerator, an exercise bike and a bathtub in his scoreboard trailer. He cooked leg of lamb up there.
Mason kept two telephones on the scoreboard in 1970, one for fans and one for reporters. His original goal was a sellout; when that looked hopeless the Brewers lowered it to 40,000.
He came down on August 16, 1970 by swinging onto the field on a 30-foot rope, which badly burned both hands. His verdict afterward: a great experience, but he would not do it again.
The published accounts of the stunt mention no pay for Mason. The closest thing to a reward was a job the next spring as a night watchman at the Brewers' training complex in Tempe, Arizona.

The 1973 home opener that was supposed to unveil the beer-barrel chalet and giant mug was snowed out. Bernie and the mug debuted instead on April 14, 1973, and the first slide celebrated a Pedro Garcia homer.
Mason never wore the costume. He died of cancer in June 1973, a few weeks after the mustachioed character built in his honor started sliding.

On July 8, 1973, Rangers manager Whitey Herzog accused Bernie of stealing signs: a man with binoculars in the chalet, supposedly there to release balloons, relayed the catcher's calls, and Bernie signaled the hitter with his arms.

The alleged spy inside the 1973 Bernie suit turned out to be Dan McCarthy, a 17-year-old Marquette student. Herzog later admitted he invented the charge to soothe rookie pitcher David Clyde after a 17-2 loss.

For Bernie's first six seasons he had a sidekick, Bonnie Brewer, whose job was to sweep the bases mid-game, kiss the visiting third-base coach on the cheek and then swat him on the backside with her broom.

Bernie's 1984 retirement was not a decision about Bernie. The Brewers rebuilt the bleachers, replaced his chalet with a speaker tower and put the chalet in storage under the third-base box seats until fans voted him back in 1993.
Bernie slides three ways: in the middle of the first inning, after every Brewers home run, and on the final out of a home win. The theoretical maximum is seven slides in a nine-inning game.
In 2007 Bernie slid 253 times in 81 home games, about 3.12 a game, the busiest season a Milwaukee Magazine count found. The slowest was 2002, at 2.15 slides a game.
The current slide, rebuilt as a chalet in 2021 during the pandemic shutdown, is 26 feet tall and 75 feet long, and the chalet sits nearly 100 feet above the field. No beer mug waits at the bottom.
In October 2019 Bernie was one of 17 mascots on the ballot for the Mascot Hall of Fame in Whiting, Indiana, an institution founded by the man who originally played the Phillie Phanatic.

Hank, the stray bichon frise mix the Brewers found at spring training in February 2014 and named after Hank Aaron, raised more than 300,000 dollars for charity through merchandise before he died in September 2024.

mascots.name: The Famous Racing Sausages
mascots.tagline: Five foam sausages, one 46-page police report

facts.fact: The Brewers VP who heard the pitch for a live sausage race in fall 1992, Gabe Paul Jr., said he did not think it would fly. His own son Jeff ran as the Polish sausage in the first race.

Michael Dillon, the graphic designer behind the race, built the first three costumes himself from foam rubber, contact cement and spray paint. The eye hole was about eight inches, and the team practiced in them exactly once.
Dillon wore green lederhosen inside the bratwurst for the first race on June 27, 1993, in honor of his German grandfather, and won. The home plate umpire complained that it made the sport a joke.

The crowd for the first live race was 45,580, there to see Paul Molitor return in a Blue Jays uniform. The animated scoreboard sausages had raced across an illustrated Milwaukee skyline to the Chariots of Fire theme.
The chorizo, number 5 and nicknamed Cinco, ran once on Cerveceros Day, July 29, 2006, then had to sit out until 2007 because MLB does not allow a team to add a new mascot in mid-season.

The chorizo was developed with Nancy Hernandez, a Latino marketing consultant, and wears a brown sombrero and yellow guayabera. When NPR asked to interview him in 2006, the Brewers declined because sausages don't talk.

Randall Simon's July 9, 2003 bat swing earned him a three-game MLB suspension, a 2,000 dollar league fine, and a 432 dollar disorderly conduct citation from the Milwaukee County sheriff. He was booked for misdemeanor battery but never charged.

Mandy Block, the 19-year-old inside the Italian sausage Simon hit, scraped a knee and asked only that he autograph the bat. She and her mother also got a trip to Curacao, Simon's home island, from its tourism office.

Guido, the Italian sausage, vanished on February 16, 2013 after a Cedarburg curling club fundraiser. The police report ran 46 pages. Two men later left the 5,000 dollar costume on a bar stool and told the bartender she saw nothing.

The sausages race Pittsburgh's pierogies in a home-and-home relay, and have run at PNC Park. A pierogi named Cheese Chester broke his foot mid-race there on July 23, 2014 and was back racing two days later.

Which sausage wins most depends on who you ask and when. A 2013 radio history said the Italian had the most career wins, and a University of Wisconsin meat science page had the Italian leading 2024 with 18.
Hank, the Brewers' stray dog, ran the sausage race on February 27, 2014 and lost. Stephen Colbert ran as the hot dog on August 20, 2021 and finished last.

mascots.name: Raymond
mascots.tagline: A blue seadog of a species that does not exist

facts.fact: Raymond's first game was June 21, 1998, a 3-1 Devil Rays loss to the Red Sox in front of a sellout crowd at Tropicana Field. He is the only mascot the franchise has had since its first game.
The official origin story is that Rays scouts on a fishing trip lured him to the boat with the smell of hot dogs, then signed him for all the hot dogs he could eat.
The Rays list Raymond as a seadog of the species Canus Manta Whatthefluffalus. There is no genus Canus; dogs are Canis, and a blogger who checked found that canus is Latin for aging, not for dog.
The team bio gives Raymond's height as tall enough to ride the rides at Disney World and his weight as 'don't worry about it.' His favorite book is One Fish Two Fish Red Fish Blue Fish.

Kelly Frank played Raymond for five seasons and perfected his butt shimmy. Three weeks after supervisors told her she had out-enthused the Phillie Phanatic in the 2008 World Series, the Rays fired her without explanation.
On April 3, 2013 a fan handed Raymond a sign joking about Steve Irwin's death by stingray, and he posed with it. The Rays apologized the next day for a lapse in judgment.

On September 10, 2013 a Red Sox fan from Needham, Massachusetts, twice reached over a railing and grabbed Raymond by the neck. Raymond had to push off him to break loose and declined to press charges.

In May 2016, a couple of weeks after losing a pregame boxing match to Dodgers Adrian Gonzalez and Kike Hernandez, Raymond knocked down the Athletics' mascot Stomper by the Oakland bullpen and declared himself King of the Mascots.

DJ Kitty began as a scoreboard video after Rays players said they were tired of the Keyboard Cat clip. The team's fan experience VP would not say whose cat it was, comparing that to unmasking Mickey Mouse.

DJ Kitty's official bio lists him at 6 feet, 200 pounds, position DDJ for designated disc jockey, found out back by the Tropicana Field dumpsters. The full-size costume debuted April 7, 2013; the Rays lost 13-0.

The Rays' cowbell habit dates to 2006, when the team played the Saturday Night Live 'more cowbell' sketch on the video board. House rules say to ring on two-strike counts against the visitors and whenever a Ray reaches base.
The Baseball Hall of Fame owns a 2001 Raymond bobblehead with two springs, a Devil Rays teal shirt and a Lykes sponsor plaque, handed out at a promotion called the Double Bobble Wobble.

texas_ties.fact: Bernie's one scandal came from the Texas Rangers. In July 1973 manager Whitey Herzog claimed the mascot was relaying stolen signs from his chalet; the kid in the suit was 17 and said he had never even stolen cookies.

Raymond's only previous World Series was played entirely in Texas. The Rays lost to the Dodgers in six games at Globe Life Field in Arlington in October 2020, the first Series held at one ballpark since 1944.

Attendance for those 2020 games in Arlington was capped at 25 percent, a total of 68,622 across six games and an average of 11,437, Coverage of the Series does not record whether Raymond made the trip.
Both the Rays and Dodgers lived in the same bubble hotel for the 2020 Series, the Four Seasons at Las Colinas. When the Rays came back to Arlington in June 2021 they checked into the same hotel.

The Rangers' own mascot, Rangers Captain, is a palomino horse introduced in 2002 who wears number 72 for the year the franchise moved to Texas. Raymond, by contrast, has no number listed anywhere in his official bio.
